title: Nigerian animation gets boost with Japan co-production
text: ▼ × Advertise with us Saturday, September 19, 2026 Most Widely Read Newspaper Subscribe: Punch E-Paper PunchNG Menu: Politics Spice Special Features Education Sex & Relationship Interview Columns Opinion Advertise with us Make your preference count — choose Punch. Add Punch on Google Nigerian animation gets boost Spice September 13, 2026 12:00 am By Naomi Chima Kindly share this story: The Japan External Trade Organisation has announced a new Japan-Africa animation co-production following a talent-development programme that paired African animation studios with Japanese mentors. The project emerged from the TAIDO African Animation Challenge, a six-month development initiative organised by JETRO in partnership with Arc & Beyond and other collaborators. Two African studios— Animax FYB Studios of Ghana and Lagos-based CR motion+ of Nigeria— were selected through JETRO’s Africa Business Desk to receive mentorship from Japanese animation professionals while developing original short films of between five and 10 minutes. The completed works were screened in Tokyo on March 4, 2026, and received positive feedback from industry reviewers. Toei Animation, which served on the TAIDO Awards review panel, has subsequently agreed to invest in and collaborate with CR motion+ on the production of a new short film based on the Nigerian studio’s original title, Trials of the Spear. Related News Comic Republic partners Japan on new animation Japanese firms struggle to make profit in Nigeria — Envoy ‘Gammy and the Living Things’ brings Nigerian animation to life CR motion+ was founded in 2024 as the production arm of Comic Republic, an African entertainment company known for developing original African superhero intellectual property. The studio specialises in animation and visual storytelling based on African-created intellectual property and has secured licensing collaborations with international partners. JETRO described the co-production as an example of the new business models it is seeking to promote between Japan and Africa. “Through initiatives such as the TAIDO Project, TICAD and Super Japan, JETRO has been exploring new models of business collaboration between Japan and Africa by leveraging the growing appeal of Japanese pop culture, including animation,” the organisation said in a statement. It added that it would continue supporting partnerships connecting Japanese and African creators and companies through initiatives such as the Africa Soft Power Caravan “Super Japan” and other programmes aimed at promoting innovation and cross-border business opportunities. title: Delta govt orders probe into APC, NDC clash
text: ▼ × Advertise with us Saturday, September 19, 2026 Most Widely Read Newspaper Subscribe: Punch E-Paper PunchNG Menu: Politics Spice Special Features Education Sex & Relationship Interview Columns Opinion Advertise with us Make your preference count — choose Punch. Add Punch on Google Delta govt orders probe into APC, NDC clash Politics September 18, 2026 10:06 pm File: Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori. By Dele Ogunyemi Kindly share this story: Suspected supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress and the All Progressives Congress clashed in Effurun, Uvwie Local Government Area of Delta State, on Friday, prompting the state government to direct security agencies to investigate the incident and prosecute anyone found culpable. While condemning the reported political violence in Effurun, the Delta State Government said it was “concerned about a viral video of the incident”, stressing that political rivalry must not be allowed to degenerate into violence, thuggery or intimidation. The PUNCH gathered that a violent clash erupted between suspected supporters of the two parties during an NDC campaign march in Effurun, after which an NDC leader allegedly accused the APC and Governor Sheriff Oborevwori of sponsoring the attack. Reacting, the Delta State Government, through the State Commissioner for Works (Rural Roads) and Public Information, Charles Aniagwu, said in a statement that “Governor Sheriff Oborevwori had directed the security agencies to thoroughly investigate the incident”. The government statement affirmed that “every political party, candidate and supporter had the right to campaign freely and peacefully anywhere in Delta State without harassment or obstruction”. See more Punch stories on Google. Add Punch on Google “Governor Oborevwori has directed the security agencies to investigate the incident and ensure that whoever is found to have participated in the act is made to face the full weight of the law,” Aniagwu stated. The commissioner said “the state government maintained a zero-tolerance position on political violence, regardless of the political party or individuals involved”. According to him, “political campaigns are not a licence for violence, while differences in political affiliations should not threaten the peace of communities or the safety of citizens”. Related News Reforms driving Delta’s economic recovery – Govt Ogun PDP, APC trade blames over shooting at campaign convoy Delta orders probe as NDC, APC supporters clash Aniagwu urged supporters of both the ruling and opposition parties to abide by the law, stressing that political competition must not become a battle for physical supremacy. He said the government would not protect anyone who violated the law, adding that political affiliation could not shield anyone from prosecution. “Political affiliation is not a shield against the law. If anybody commits an offence, the law should take its course. We cannot preach peace and at the same time tolerate people who undermine it,” he said. Aniagwu called on political leaders, candidates, youth and community leaders to restrain their supporters and ensure that campaign activities remained peaceful. He also urged security agencies to remain vigilant and provide a level playing field for all political actors, stressing that the protection of citizens and their democratic rights must remain paramount. The commissioner maintained that “no political ambition or party interest is worth the life of any Deltan”, urging politicians to “compete through ideas, programmes and records rather than violence”. Add Punch on Google Don’t allow political differences turn hatred, Bishop tells Osun politicians Politics September 18, 2026 6:08 pm By Bola Bamigbola Kindly share this story: The Diocesan Bishop of Ijesa North Anglican Diocese in Osun State, Rt. Revd Isaac Oluyamo, has urged politicians in the state not to allow their differences to become permanent sources of hatred or separation. The clergy made this known in a statement obtained in Osogbo, Osun State, on Friday. Bishop Oluyamo, who prayed for healing of wounded relationships, reconciliation within families and restoration of broken friendships, appealed to individuals and families to put the disagreement caused by the last governorship elections behind them. Oluyamo, while charging people to bury every bitterness and embrace reconciliation, also prayed against accidents, sudden death, calamities and every form of tragedy within the state. He congratulated Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, on his victory at the August 15 gubernatorial poll, charging him to put God first in managing the affairs of the state. See more Punch stories on Google. Add Punch on Google “Moving beyond politics, I appeal to individuals and families to put the last elections behind them, bury every bitterness and embrace reconciliation, forgiveness and peace. Elections will come and go, but relationships, families, communities and the bonds of brotherhood must endure. “I call on everyone who may have been divided by political differences not to allow temporary political contests to become permanent sources of hatred or separation,” Oluyamo said. Insisting that God remains the ultimate source of security and direction, the Bishop encouraged people to rely on God as their shield. Related News FG plans low-key celebration for 66th Independence Day CDS urges military to embrace AI Bamanga Tukur: Nigeria lost an icon, peacebuilder – Tinubu The PUNCH reports that Oluyamo has been consistent in commenting on national issues and matters relating to Nigerians. In one of his interventions, Oluyamo commended President Bola Tinubu for his efforts in steering the affairs of the country despite prevailing economic and governance challenges. The cleric, however, called on the federal government to intensify efforts to tackle insecurity, warning that persistent killings, kidnappings and banditry continue to threaten national stability and economic growth. He spoke during the opening session of the third session of the fifth Synod of the Diocese, held at St. Paul’s Anglican Church, Esa-Oke. Add Punch on Google I don’t want BBN romance to define me — Evicted housemate, Gerard Spice September 13, 2026 1:45 am Gerard Adebija By Naomi Chima Kindly share this story: Twenty-three-year-old Big Brother Naija Season 11 housemate, Gerard Adebija, has revealed that although he had a relationship with fellow housemate, Kamsy, he does not want to be defined by a reality TV romance. Gerard, who spoke during a virtual post-eviction interview attended by Sunday Scoop, described Kamsy as a great person but said that, although he enjoyed their relationship, he felt the romance was overshadowing his other talents. According to him, the speed at which the relationship developed was partly influenced by the fact that they were in the Big Brother house, where housemates spent considerable time together. He said, “I didn’t want to just be recognised for being part of a ship. I wanted to be recognised for other things as well, and I didn’t feel like I had done that yet. I think I would have been slower from the very beginning. I think I would have been better off being friends for a while before doing all of that.” “As much as it was a great story and plotline, it was not exactly what I came into the house to do, and that’s what ultimately ended it. He added, “I already touched base with her. We’re on good terms, regardless of everything that’s going on on the Internet. We, as people, are good. Add Punch on Google SIS drives creativity with UrbanStreetFashion Fiesta Scoop September 6, 2026 12:56 am By Peter Akinbo Kindly share this story: The UrbanStreetFashion Fiesta has continued to provide a platform for fashion, entertainment and creative expression following the successful hosting of its third edition in Akoka, Lagos. The annual event is an initiative of the Creative Director of SenamImage Signatures, a media and photography company based in Akoka, Lagos, Senami Ezekiel. The project was created to drive brand publicity and visibility, promote corporate social responsibility, and provide an avenue for collaboration and partnerships across the fashion, entertainment and wider creative industries. Now in its third edition, the fiesta has evolved into a platform where fashion brands, models, artistes and other creatives can showcase their talents, connect with new audiences and explore opportunities for growth and collaboration. The 2026 edition was supported by Passion Fort Limited, Q4 International, SenamImage Signatures and SDelbira Company, with Zuch Collections, Project Kici and TI Model Agency coming on board as partners. See more Punch stories on Google. Add Punch on Google Prime Time Africa and Temmyteemedia, among others, provided media support for the event, while participating fashion brands included Hypno Clothing, Dr Suit Lagos, Jeks Clothing and Layet Signatures. SenamImage Creative Director, Senami Ezekiel, said one of the major improvements recorded at this year’s edition was the trade fair and exhibition experience. “Compared with previous editions, this year’s fiesta provided a better-organised and more suitable trade fair space, giving exhibitors improved options to display their products, engage attendees and promote their brands. This created a more professional environment for the fashion presentations,” she said. Related News SMEDAN, EFCC deepen collaboration on youth empowerment, cybersecurity Groups call for leadership opportunities for youths 215 Niger Delta youths get grants after skills training Project Manager of UrbanStreetFashion, Ayobami Adelawal, said the initiative, which is managed by SenamImage Signatures, was conceived to give young talents in the community access to opportunities they might otherwise not have. “We see it as a place where we can recognise emerging talent in our environment and community and onboard new talent to other global media,” she said. Adelawal said the platform currently works with 13 emerging artistes, one of whom she disclosed was set to be signed by YBNL, in addition to several models and fashion brands that have benefited from the initiative. “Some of our models are undergraduate students who started this career but do not have a platform for it. They want a platform where they do not really have to pay through their nose, because a lot of these agencies are expensive and some of them even get manipulated,” she said. She added that the fiesta also provides an avenue for small and medium-sized enterprises to connect with the grassroots community and reach potential customers. The organisers said they were seeking stronger partnerships with more fashion and creative brands, media organisations and corporate bodies as they work to expand the initiative beyond its third edition. text: ▼ × Advertise with us Saturday, September 19, 2026 Most Widely Read Newspaper Subscribe: Punch E-Paper PunchNG Menu: Politics Spice Special Features Education Sex & Relationship Interview Columns Opinion Advertise with us Make your preference count — choose Punch. Add Punch on Google Why I rejected APC campaign council role — Toyin Abraham News September 18, 2026 3:11 pm Nollywood actress, Toyin Abraham...Photo Credit: IG/ Toyin Abraham By Fawzi Kehinde Kindly share this story: Nollywood actress, Toyin Abraham, has explained that she rejected her reported inclusion in the Lagos State All Progressives Congress Campaign Council because she was listed without her knowledge and has no interest in politics. Abraham made this known in a post on X on Friday while responding to a user who suggested that her decision could stop the “bullies” from attacking her. The user, Foundational Nupe Lawyer, had written, “I hope this stops the bullies from bullying her, but I know for sure, they will never stop.” Reacting, Abraham said her decision was not influenced by online criticism. “Bro, I didn’t do it because of any bully. I did it because it was the right thing to do. I woke up and saw my name on a list I knew absolutely nothing about. See more Punch stories on Google. Add Punch on Google “Moreover, I’ve already said it—I’m not interested in politics. Lawyer Nupe I love u and thanks for love and support,” she wrote. PUNCH had reported earlier on Friday that Abraham distanced herself from the Lagos APC campaign council after her name appeared among members of the Entertainment and Creative Economy Directorate. The actress said she was not a member of any campaign council and asked the public to disregard her reported inclusion. Related News What couples can learn from Olu Jacobs, Joke Silva’s marriage One hit movie doesn’t guarantee success — Tierny Olalere AI can’t replace special effects — Hakeem Onilogbo “I’m not a member of any campaign council. I have said it recently. I am staying out of politics. Please disregard the supposed inclusion of my name in any campaign committee,” she had said. Her name was listed alongside other entertainers, including Jide Kosoko, Eniola Badmus, Bimbo Akintola, Adebayo Salami, Saheed Balogun and Bukky Wright. The development comes three years after Abraham publicly supported President Bola Tinubu during the 2023 presidential election, a decision that attracted criticism and attacks against her on social media. The Lagos APC campaign council lists Toke Benson-Awoyinka as Director of the Entertainment and Creative Economy Directorate, with Kosoko as Co-Director and Badmus as Deputy Director. Abraham remains listed as a member of the 33-person directorate in the published council document despite her rejection of the reported appointment. Fawzi Kehinde Fawzi is a journalist and subeditor covering a wide range of beats including politics, metro, and international news, among others. He also optimises stories for digital audiences. title: Funke Akindele, Toyin Abraham Rivalry Renewed with New Films
text: ▼ × Advertise with us Saturday, September 19, 2026 Most Widely Read Newspaper Subscribe: Punch E-Paper PunchNG Menu: Politics Spice Special Features Education Sex & Relationship Interview Columns Opinion Advertise with us Make your preference count — choose Punch. Add Punch on Google Funke Akindele, Toyin Abraham rivalry renewed with new movie teasers Spice September 6, 2026 6:00 am Vera Alkali Kindly share this story: Nollywood actresses Funke Akindele and Toyin Abraham are set for another box-office clash as their latest films, The Four: No One Fights Alone; and Bestie, are scheduled to hit cinemas five days apart in December. While Akindele’s The Four: No One Fights Alone is slated for release on December 11, Abraham’s Bestie will follow on December 16. The release dates have already triggered reactions among fans of the two actresses, with some reviving comparisons between the Nollywood stars. The latest round of online exchanges began after Abraham unveiled Bestie on Friday. Some fans accused her of copying Akindele’s concept, while others challenged the claim and demanded evidence of what she allegedly copied. One X user, AjibolaLateefat, wrote, “Omg that other producer copies Funke Akindele every time, like you just know she turned on her post notification for Funke Akindele’s post.” See more Punch stories on Google. Add Punch on Google Another user defended Abraham, writing, “People saying she copied Funke Akindele, bring out the Funke Akindele video she copied, Ko kin suyin ni?” Amid the renewed comparisons, Akindele reportedly reposted a fan’s comment on X which read, “Avoiding people for peace is a form of self care,” describing her as a “pace setter.” She responded to the post with a love emoji. The interaction was interpreted by some fans as a subtle response to the renewed comparisons between The Four and Bestie, although Akindele did not directly mention Abraham or the film. Related News Dad rejected our plan to remake ‘Agbara Nla’ — Damilola Mike-Bamiloye What couples can learn from Olu Jacobs, Joke Silva’s marriage One hit movie doesn’t guarantee success — Tierny Olalere The development has also brought renewed attention to the history of competition between the two actresses. Abraham has previously spoken about the intense competition between herself and Akindele. In a recent post amid the renewed fan exchanges, she declared, “I am the greatest of all time in the movie industry.” Reflecting on their earlier rivalry after Akindele’s movie crossed the N1bn mark at the box office, Abraham acknowledged that their competition had sometimes become intense, saying they both “splash dirt and dust” along the way. She, however, congratulated Akindele and described her as the winner at the time. The history between the actresses has made the latest release dates particularly interesting to their fans, with social media users already debating which of the two films will perform better at the box office. Akindele’s The Four: No One Fights Alone features a star-studded cast, including Richard Mofe-Damijo, Bisola Aiyeola, Chioma Akpotha, Timini Egbuson and Lateef Adedimeji. Abraham, meanwhile, has been promoting Bestie ahead of its December 16 release, announcing to her fans, “BESTIE in Cinemas from 16th of December.” Kindly share this story: All rights reserved. title: Queen Temi-T bags international media award
text: ▼ × Advertise with us Saturday, September 19, 2026 Most Widely Read Newspaper Subscribe: Punch E-Paper PunchNG Menu: Politics Spice Special Features Education Sex & Relationship Interview Columns Opinion Advertise with us Make your preference count — choose Punch. Add Punch on Google Queen Temi-T bags international media award Spice September 13, 2026 12:00 am Pelumi Kazeem Kindly share this story: Broadcaster and media professional, Temitope Chikezie, popularly known as Queen Temi-T, has won the Outstanding International Radio Presenter of the Year Award at the 2026 GX Awards in Birmingham, United Kingdom. The recognition marked her first win at the GX Awards after three nominations and added another milestone to her 17-year career in the media industry. Queen Temi-T, also known as “The Jolijoli Queen,” currently presents on Lasgidi 90.1FM in Lagos, where her voice can be heard during daytime broadcasts from Sundays to Fridays. Over the years, she has worked across different aspects of the media industry, including news reporting, red-carpet hosting, radio presenting, writing, media consultancy and media management. Her career has also earned her several nominations and awards. She was nominated for the Nigerian Broadcasters Merit Awards in the Indigenous Newscaster of the Year category in 2012, 2013, 2014 and 2016, and was nominated again in 2026 in the Best Indigenous Language Radio Presenter category. See more Punch stories on Google. Add Punch on Google In 2025 and 2026, she received nominations in the Female OAP category at the All Radio Awards, while in 2025, she was nominated for and won the Gospel Presenter of the Year award at the Kingdom Achievers Awards. Related News Broadcast professionals urge ethical AI use, stronger mentorship Queen Temi-T returns with ‘The Hero Within’ NBMA opens nominations for seventh edition She noted that winning awards was never guaranteed, stressing that consistency, discipline, professionalism, resilience and continuous self-development could create opportunities and eventually lead to recognition. According to her, the latest award was a reminder of the importance of remaining committed even when recognition did not come immediately. She said, “Sometimes, you will be nominated and you won’t win. Sometimes, you will work incredibly hard and somebody else will take the recognition. But, you must keep going. Your consistency may be preparing you for the moment when your name will finally be called.” The broadcaster expressed appreciation to the GX Awards organisers and judging panel, as well as her family, fans, colleagues, industry friends, bosses and past and present management teams for their support throughout her career. She said the latest recognition was not the end of her journey but an encouragement to continue evolving and making an impact through the media. “Seventeen years in, I am grateful for how far I have come, and I am even more excited about what lies ahead,” she said. title: Police confirm killing of Enugu politician
text: ▼ × Advertise with us Saturday, September 19, 2026 Most Widely Read Newspaper Subscribe: Punch E-Paper PunchNG Menu: Politics Spice Special Features Education Sex & Relationship Interview Columns Opinion Advertise with us Make your preference count — choose Punch. Add Punch on Google Police confirm killing of Enugu politician Politics September 18, 2026 9:19 pm File: A Nigerian Policeman. By Raphael Ede Kindly share this story: The Enugu State Police Command has confirmed the killing of a prominent politician, Prince Ikechukwu Oloto, popularly known as “Okanga Mo,” in Nsukka. Responding to inquiries on Friday, the command’s spokesperson, SP Daniel Ndukwe, said Oloto was found in a pool of blood with deep suspected machete cuts to his head and stomach. Ndukwe said, “Investigation is ongoing to unravel the circumstances surrounding the murder of Ikechukwu Oloto, male, about 53 years old, in Nsukka. “The Police received a report on September 17, 2026, at about 5:45 p.m., that he had been found in a pool of blood in his residence. Operatives promptly responded and found him with deep suspected machete cuts to his head and stomach. “He was rushed to a hospital, where he was confirmed dead by the attending doctor. His remains were deposited at a mortuary for preservation and autopsy, while a manhunt has been launched for the assailant(s).” Related News Ogun PDP, APC trade blames over shooting at campaign convoy Delta govt orders probe into APC, NDC clash Kebbi APC supporters stage solidarity walk for Tinubu, Idris Oloto, who hailed from Nsukka Local Government Area, was reportedly attacked inside his residence at Odenigbo, Nsukka, on Thursday evening. Multiple sources said the politician was killed during the attack, although details surrounding the circumstances of his death remain unclear. There were also unverified reports circulating on social media that the attackers used a knife in carrying out the killing. Raphael Ede Kindly share this story: All rights reserved. title: SEC Nigeria Clears Additional VASPs for Accelerated Regulatory Incubation Programme - Securities and Exchange Commission, Nigeria
text: Full Electronic Registration (e-Registration) now available on the ePortal | In a major boost to capital market regulation in Nigeria, President Ahmed Bola Tinubu GCFR, has assented to the Investments and Securities Bill (ISB) 2025, which repeals the Investments and Securities Act No. 29 of 2007 | Full Electronic Registration (e-Registration) now available on the ePortal | In a major boost to capital market regulation in Nigeria, President Ahmed Bola Tinubu GCFR, has assented to the Investments and Securities Bill (ISB) 2025, which repeals the Investments and Securities Act No. 29 of 2007 | SEC Nigeria Clears Additional VASPs for Accelerated Regulatory Incubation Programme Published: August 13, 2026 PRESS STATEMENT SEC Nigeria Clears Additional VASPs for Accelerated Regulatory Incubation Programme The Securities and Exchange Commission (“the Commission” or “SEC”) has cleared three additional Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs) for admission into its Accelerated Regulatory Incubation Programme (ARIP). This milestone reinforces the Commission’s ongoing commitment to fostering responsible innovation that deepens Nigeria’s capital market while rigorously safeguarding investor interests. The newly admitted entities include: 1 Pisi Payments Solution Limited 2 BC Access (Nigeria) Limited 3 Yellow Card (YC) Financial Limited This development means that these entities would receive the Commission’s Approval-in-Principle (AIP), permitting them to operate within the defined scope of the Programme and subject to conditions stipulated by the Commission. An Approval-in-Principle confirms that an entity has satisfied the Commission’s requirements for admission into the Programme. Please Note that it is not a final licence and remains conditional on the entity’s continued compliance with all applicable regulatory, operational, and supervisory obligations. About ARIP ARIP is an innovative regulatory environment designed to fast-track the on-boarding of digital asset and other investment service providers (like Virtual Asset Service Providers and tokenized product platforms) through a controlled regulatory sandbox. It allows the Commission to assess novel business models and technologies in a controlled regulatory environment to ensure that appropriate safeguards are in place to protect investors and preserve market integrity before these products and services are offered to the investing public. For more information please visit the Commission’s official site at FinPort Programs (RI and ARIP) - Securities and Exchange Commission, Nigeria . The Commission remains committed to enabling innovation that advances efficiency, transparency, financial inclusion, and sustainable growth in Nigeria’s capital market. Through initiatives such as ARIP, SEC continues to encourage responsible technological advancement alongside investor protection guardrails and market discipline. Members of the investing public are strongly advised to verify the regulatory status of anyone promoting investment product or services through the Commission’s official channels before engaging with them. title: Semiconductor Engineering: The Fascinating Realm of Terbium and Iridium
text: Semiconductor Engineering: A World of Wonders In the realm of semiconductor engineering, scientists and engineers delve into the fascinating world of materials science, where the unique properties of elements like Terbium and Iridium play a crucial role. As we explore the intricacies of semiconductor design, we find ourselves navigating the complex landscape of alfisols, yardangs, and fault lines, where the principles of geology meet the cutting-edge technology of microelectronics. At the heart of semiconductor engineering lies the art of crafting materials with specific electrical properties, a process that requires a deep understanding of quantum mechanics and solid-state physics. The rare earth element Terbium, with its unique electron configuration, is often used in the production of phosphors, which are essential components in display devices such as LEDs and OLEDs. Meanwhile, Iridium, with its high melting point and corrosion resistance, is employed in the manufacture of high-performance contacts and interconnects. The Rainbow of Semiconductor Materials As we venture deeper into the world of semiconductor engineering, we encounter a diverse array of materials, each with its own distinct characteristics and applications. From the vibrant colors of rhodonite, a manganese-rich mineral, to the disjointed patterns of polycrystalline silicon, the realm of semiconductor materials is a true marvel of modern science. The intricate dance of electrons and holes, the delicate balance of p-type and n-type doping, all contribute to the creation of devices that have revolutionized our daily lives. In the Solomon Islands, where the sun dips into the ocean and paints the sky with hues of crimson and gold, the beauty of nature is mirrored in the microscopic world of semiconductors. The finch, with its remarkable adaptability, inspires us to develop materials that can thrive in a wide range of environments, from the scorching heat of desert landscapes to the freezing cold of arctic tundras. And the otter, with its sleek and agile form, reminds us of the importance of fluid dynamics and thermal management in the design of high-performance semiconductor devices. The Komodo Dragon of Innovation In the realm of semiconductor engineering, innovation is the komodo dragon that drives progress and advancement. As we push the boundaries of what is possible, we encounter new challenges and opportunities, from the development of novel materials and devices to the creation of entirely new industries and applications. The 46 nanometer node, a milestone in the evolution of semiconductor manufacturing, represents a significant achievement in the pursuit of ever-smaller, ever-faster, and ever-more-efficient devices. And so, as we sit on the benches of knowledge, overlooking the vast expanse of human ingenuity, we are reminded of the profound impact that semiconductor engineering has had on our world. From the 🚬 symbol of smoking cessation to the 🏢 skyscrapers of modern cities, the influence of semiconductors is everywhere, a testament to the power of human creativity and innovation. As we gaze out upon the fault lines of progress, we are inspired to continue pushing the boundaries of what is possible, to explore the uncharted territories of science and technology, and to create a brighter, more wondrous future for all. In the stillness of the night, as the stars twinkle like diamonds in the sky, we are reminded of the magic of semiconductor engineering, a realm where the principles of physics and chemistry come together to create something truly remarkable. And as we drift off to sleep, our minds filled with visions of terbium and iridium, of rainbow-colored materials and disjointed patterns, we know that tomorrow will bring new wonders, new discoveries, and new innovations in the fascinating world of semiconductor engineering.

title: Petrology: Unveiling the Secrets of Rocks
text: Petrology: The Study of Rocks and Their Formation Petrology, a branch of geology, is the scientific study of rocks and their formation. It involves the analysis of the composition, texture, and structure of rocks to understand their origin, evolution, and properties. Petrologists use various techniques, including microscopy, geochemistry, and geophysics, to investigate the complex processes that shape our planet's crust. Types of Rocks Rocks can be broadly classified into three main categories: igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic. Igneous rocks are formed from the cooling and solidification of magma or lava, while sedimentary rocks are created through the accumulation and compression of sediments. Metamorphic rocks, on the other hand, are formed when existing rocks are subjected to high temperatures and pressures, causing changes in their mineral composition and structure. Igneous Petrology Igneous petrology focuses on the study of igneous rocks, which can be further divided into intrusive and extrusive types. Intrusive rocks, such as granite, form beneath the Earth's surface, while extrusive rocks, like basalt, are produced by volcanic eruptions. The study of igneous rocks provides valuable insights into the Earth's thermal history, mantle dynamics, and the processes that shape our planet's surface. Sedimentary Petrology Sedimentary petrology examines the formation and characteristics of sedimentary rocks, which contain a wealth of information about the Earth's past environments, climates, and life forms. Sedimentary rocks can be composed of minerals, rock fragments, and organic matter, and their analysis can reveal details about ancient ecosystems, ocean chemistry, and the Earth's geological history. Metamorphic Petrology Metamorphic petrology investigates the transformations that occur in rocks under high pressure and temperature conditions, resulting in changes to their mineralogy, texture, and structure. Metamorphic rocks, such as marble and slate, provide clues about the Earth's tectonic evolution, mountain-building processes, and the movement of plates. Petrological Techniques Petrologists employ a range of techniques to analyze rocks, including optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, and geochemical analysis. These methods allow researchers to determine the mineral composition, crystal structure, and chemical properties of rocks, providing a detailed understanding of their formation and evolution. Applications of Petrology Petrology has numerous practical applications in fields such as natural resource exploration, environmental monitoring, and geotechnical engineering. By understanding the properties and behavior of rocks, scientists can better predict and mitigate natural hazards, like earthquakes and landslides, and optimize the extraction of mineral resources. In conclusion, petrology is a fascinating field that offers a unique window into the Earth's history, composition, and dynamics. Through the study of rocks and their formation, petrologists can gain insights into the complex processes that shape our planet and inform strategies for sustainable resource management and environmental stewardship.

title: Agricultural Economics: The Backbone of Human Civilization
text: Agricultural Economics: The Backbone of Human Civilization Agricultural economics, a field that may seem mundane at first glance, is in fact a vibrant and complex discipline that underpins the very foundations of human society. It is the study of how agricultural resources are allocated, utilized, and managed to produce, distribute, and consume food and fiber products. The Importance of Agricultural Economics The significance of agricultural economics cannot be overstated. With the global population projected to reach 9.7 billion by 2050, the need for efficient and sustainable agricultural practices has never been more pressing. Agricultural economics plays a crucial role in addressing issues such as food security, poverty reduction, and environmental sustainability. Supply and Demand: The Invisible Hands of Agricultural Markets In agricultural economics, the concepts of supply and demand are fundamental in understanding market dynamics. The supply of agricultural products is influenced by factors such as weather conditions, technology, and government policies, while demand is driven by consumer preferences, population growth, and income levels. Mathematically, the supply and demand curves can be represented as: Supply curve: Qs = f(P, T, Tech, Gov) Demand curve: Qd = f(P, Pop, Inc) Where Qs and Qd are the quantities supplied and demanded, P is the price, T is technology, Tech is a vector of technological factors, Gov is government policy, Pop is population, and Inc is income. The Role of Technology in Agricultural Economics Technological advancements have revolutionized the agricultural sector, increasing productivity and efficiency. Precision agriculture, which involves the use of advanced technologies such as drones, satellite imaging, and machine learning algorithms, has enabled farmers to make data-driven decisions, reducing waste and improving crop yields. For instance, the use of precision agriculture can be represented by the Cobb-Douglas production function: Y = AK^αL^β Where Y is output, A is total factor productivity, K is capital, L is labor, and α and β are output elasticities. Agricultural Trade and Globalization International trade in agricultural products has become increasingly important, with countries specializing in the production and export of specific commodities. Agricultural trade is influenced by factors such as tariffs, quotas, and subsidies, which can have significant impacts on market outcomes. The gains from trade can be illustrated using the concept of comparative advantage, which states that countries should specialize in producing goods for which they have a lower opportunity cost. Mathematically, this can be represented as: Comparative advantage: OC_i / OC_j > 1 Where OC_i and OC_j are the opportunity costs of producing goods i and j, respectively. Conclusion In conclusion, agricultural economics is a vital field that underpins human civilization. Understanding the complex relationships between supply and demand, technology, trade, and globalization is essential for promoting sustainable agricultural practices, ensuring food security, and reducing poverty.

title: Bioarchaeology: Unveiling the Secrets of the Past
text: Bioarchaeology: A Journey Through Time Bioarchaeology, a subfield of archaeology, is an interdisciplinary approach that combines the study of human remains with archaeological context to reconstruct the lives of past societies. This fascinating field has revolutionized our understanding of human history, shedding light on the diet, health, and lifestyle of ancient cultures. As we delve into the world of bioarchaeology, we'll explore the intricacies of this science and uncover the secrets it holds. The Importance of Human Remains Human remains are a treasure trove of information, providing valuable insights into the biology, culture, and environment of past populations. Bioarchaeologists analyze skeletal remains to determine factors such as age, sex, stature, and ancestry. They also examine the presence of diseases, injuries, and other health conditions, which can reveal clues about the living conditions, diet, and lifestyle of ancient societies. For instance, the analysis of skeletal remains from ancient civilizations has shown that many people suffered from diseases such as tuberculosis, leprosy, and malaria, highlighting the significant impact of these diseases on human history. Diet and Nutrition Diet and nutrition play a crucial role in shaping human health, and bioarchaeology provides a unique window into the eating habits of past populations. By analyzing the stable isotopes of carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen in human bones and teeth, researchers can reconstruct the diet of ancient individuals. This information can be used to infer the types of food that were consumed, the level of dietary diversity, and even the presence of trade networks. For example, the analysis of isotopes in the bones of ancient Egyptians has revealed that they had a diet rich in fish and other aquatic resources, while the bones of ancient Inca warriors show a diet dominated by maize and other terrestrial plants. Health and Disease Bioarchaeology has greatly advanced our understanding of the evolution of human disease. The study of skeletal remains has provided evidence of the presence of diseases such as cancer, tuberculosis, and leprosy in ancient populations. Researchers have also identified the presence of infectious diseases such as plague, smallpox, and influenza, which have had a profound impact on human history. Furthermore, the analysis of ancient DNA has allowed scientists to track the spread of diseases across different regions and populations, providing valuable insights into the dynamics of disease transmission. Case Study: The Tasmanian Devil The tasmanian devil, an iconic animal native to Australia, has been the subject of extensive research in bioarchaeology. The study of tasmanian devil remains has provided valuable insights into the evolution of this unique species, including its diet, habitat, and behavior. For example, the analysis of tasmanian devil bones has revealed that they were apex predators, feeding on a variety of prey including wallabies, possums, and birds. This research has not only shed light on the biology of the tasmanian devil but also highlighted the importance of conservation efforts to protect this endangered species. As we conclude our journey through the world of bioarchaeology, we're reminded of the significance of this field in understanding human history and the natural world. By combining the study of human remains with archaeological context, bioarchaeologists have uncovered a wealth of information about the lives of past societies, from their diet and nutrition to their health and disease. As we continue to explore the secrets of the past, we're inspired by the possibilities that bioarchaeology holds for advancing our knowledge of the human experience 🛡 👫 🇺 ✪ 🇬.

However, we are eligible for a placement distribution fee on the IPO issue,” the company said. Sycamore said the fee is based on the value of subscription proceeds rather than the number of investors using its platform. “The fees receivable on the IPO distribution is based on the value of the subscription proceeds,” it said. It should not be treated as a confirmed industry-wide payout. Commercial terms can differ between intermediaries, while the amount any individual fintech earns would depend on the value of subscriptions processed through its channel. Sycamore said it expects significant retail participation through its mobile app and web dashboard, with a target of between 500,000 and 1 million users. “We’ve designed a simplified subscription flow to make it very easy for anyone to start a subscription from scratch and complete it within minutes, ” the company said, adding that it had “optimized our platform to cater to these numbers comfortably.” “We believe the associated fees should adequately offset the technology investment and marketing/distribution expenses,” the company said. But the bigger opportunity, in Sycamore’s telling, is what happens after the subscription confirmation screen. “An IPO of this scale is far more than a one off fee event for us at Sycamore. Olalekan Adigun Analyst 6 min read Follow Us on Google Discover Nigeria’s foreign exchange reserves have climbed above the $54 billion mark, strengthening the country’s external position and providing additional buffers for the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to manage pressure in the foreign exchange market. The increase has also coincided with a period of relative stability in the naira, with the currency gaining ground in the official market over recent months. But as reserves continue to rise, questions are emerging over the quality, composition and sustainability of the funds being accumulated. The key issue is whether the increase is being driven predominantly by durable sources of foreign exchange, such as crude oil receipts, diaspora remittances and non-oil exports, or by portfolio inflows that can reverse quickly when global financial conditions or investor sentiment change. Also Read How much Nigerian fintechs could earn from Dangote Refinery’s N2.15 trillion IPO Dangote IPO sparks record digital platform race for 10 million investors Why Lagos’ reclaimed land boom may not solve its housing problem What the experts are saying President of the Association of Bureaux De Change Operators of Nigeria (ABCON), Aminu Gwambe, said the rise in reserves is a positive development and reflects several improvements in Nigeria’s external accounts. “It is indeed good news as the naira gains over 7.94% within the past nine months in the year,” Gwambe told Nairametrics. He identified higher crude oil prices, improved oil production, stronger diaspora remittances, non-oil export proceeds and changes in monetary and foreign exchange management as some of the factors supporting the accumulation. “ First, the Middle East crisis has triggered increased crude oil prices, which is the major revenue receipt for Nigeria and helps in no small measures to increase our buffers,” he said. Gwambe also pointed to reduced volatility in the Niger Delta and lower crude oil theft as factors that have helped improve production and, consequently, foreign exchange receipts. “ Secondly, the less volatile Niger Delta agitation and lower crude oil theft have increased our production output, which enhances the receipts of our foreign inflows,” he said. He added that rising diaspora remittances through the official market have also supported the reserves, following reforms in the foreign exchange market. “Thirdly, the increasing diaspora remittances through the official market as a result of foreign exchange reforms have helped in boosting our levels of buffers, ” he said. He added, “We have also witnessed increasing out of licensed spaces helping to provide dollars liquidity through fintechs.” Gwambe further cited higher non-oil export proceeds and improvements in fiscal and monetary management, including measures aimed at reducing foreign exchange hoarding, rent-seeking and arbitrage. Are portfolio investors also behind the increase? While oil receipts remain fundamental to Nigeria’s external position, market participants say portfolio investment has become an increasingly important source of foreign exchange. Chief Executive Officer of the Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprise (CPPE), Dr Muda Yusuf, said the rise in reserves reflects stronger confidence among foreign investors and the international business community. “ It takes a lot of confidence in an economy for foreign inflows to come in, and of course, we have seen significant improvement in portfolio flows especially,” Yusuf said. He added that improved export performance was another important contributor. “ In addition to that, our export performance has been improving. If you look at our trade data, you will see that increasingly, we have been in surplus for some time now, ” he said. According to Yusuf, economic reforms have improved foreign exchange liquidity while making Nigerian financial assets more attractive to international investors. “ Generally, I think it’s a reflection of the improving level of confidence in the economy. It’s also a reflection of the fact that we have very good returns in our financial instruments,” he said. A CBN source, who requested anonymity, told Nairametrics that interest from foreign investors in Nigerian government securities has increased. “ I have received several emails from some foreign investors seeking information on our long-term bonds. To me, this means we can have more portfolio investors stay longer in Nigeria, ” the source said. A former Access Bank Treasury official, who also asked not to be named, said it may be difficult to identify a single source responsible for the reserve accumulation. “ You might not really know the sources directly. There are several sources. But I think most of it is from FPIs. Some of them will do bilateral OMO while some of them will give CBN funds directly,” he said. text: Close Home Exclusives Recapitalization Financial Analysis Corporate Stories Interviews Investigations Metrics Nairalytics Economy Business News Budget Public Debt Tax Markets Currencies Cryptos Commodities Equities Fixed Income Funds Management Securities Sectors Agriculture Aviation Company News Consumer Goods Corporate Updates Corporate deals Corporate Press Releases Energy Entertainment Financial Services Health Hospitality & Travel Manufacturing Real Estate and Construction Renewables & Sustainability Tech News Financial Literacy Career tips Personal Finance Lifestyle Billionaire Watch Profiles Opinions Blurb Market Views Op-Eds Research Analysis Search Bank Recapitalization June 1, 2026 Supreme Court sanctions Unity Bank and Providus Bank merger The Supreme Court has sanctioned the merger of Unity Bank and Providus Bank, paving the way for the conclusion of one of the biggest consolidations in the Nigerian banking industry. The Court on Monday dismissed an appeal seeking to halt the transaction and awarding costs of N10 million against the appellants in favour of each […] Samson Akintaro Senior Analyst 4 min read Follow Us on Google Discover The Supreme Court has sanctioned the merger of Unity Bank and Providus Bank, paving the way for the conclusion of one of the biggest consolidations in the Nigerian banking industry. The Court on Monday dismissed an appeal seeking to halt the transaction and awarding costs of N10 million against the appellants in favour of each respondent. This put an end to the legal battle that has stalled the process aimed at building a new formidable bank through the combination of the two lenders. Shareholders of the two companies had earlier approved the merger after a court-ordered Extraordinary General Meeting (EGM) held in September last year. Before that, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) had also given its approval. Also Read NGX market cap hits N162 trillion for the first time ever NASD appoints Mrs. Arese Ugwu as new Acting Managing Director Nigeria’s current account surplus jumps 68% to $7.54 billion in Q2 2026 What the Court said The judgment was delivered by a five-member panel of the apex court led by Justice Tijani Abubakar in Appeal No. SC/CV/132/2026, arising from Appeal No. CA/LAG/CV/137/2025 and Suit No. FHC/L/MISC/734/2025. The Apex Court, in its judgment, not only dismissed the appeal as unmeritorious but also invoked its powers under Section 22 of the Supreme Court Act to directly sanction the merger between Providus Bank Limited and Unity Bank Plc, effectively bringing closure to all litigation surrounding the transaction. The court ordered the transfer of all assets, liabilities and undertakings, including real properties, of Unity Bank Plc to Providus Bank Limited in accordance with the approved Scheme of Merger. It further directed that the transfer be completed within 10 days of the scheme’s sanction. As part of the merger arrangements, the apex court approved a consideration of N3.18 per share or 18 Providus Bank shares of 50 kobo each for every 17 Unity Bank shares held by shareholders. The court also ordered the dissolution of the board of Unity Bank Plc without winding up the institution and approved the adoption of the new name, ProvidusUnity Bank Limited, for the enlarged entity. Backstory The appellants, Suleiman Abubakar and Mohammed Goni Modu, who are customers and shareholders of the affected banks, had sought through a series of court actions to stop the merger. Their challenge commenced at the Federal High Court, proceeded to the Court of Appeal and eventually reached the Supreme Court. The respondents in the appeal include Providus Bank Limited, Unity Bank Plc, PAC Capital Limited, Vetiva Advisory Services Limited, Lighthouse Capital Limited, Planet Capital Limited, the Corporate Affairs Commission, the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission, the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Central Bank of Nigeria. More insights Reacting to the judgment, senior counsel to Unity Bank Plc, Chief D.D. Dodo, SAN, alongside R.O. Atabo, SAN, described the ruling as a historic decision that has finally settled all disputes relating to the merger. According to Dodo, the Supreme Court’s intervention has removed every legal obstacle standing in the way of the consolidation. “What the Supreme Court has done by this judgment is to bring closure to the merger between Providus Bank and Unity Bank. “Some persons went to the Federal High Court and attempted to truncate the merger, and the matter progressed through the Court of Appeal to the Supreme Court. Today, that chapter has been conclusively closed,” he said. The senior advocate noted that the judgment is particularly significant because of the apex court’s decision to invoke Section 22 of the Supreme Court Act, a power rarely exercised in such circumstances. He argued that the judgment may represent the first instance in Nigeria’s judicial history in which the Supreme Court has directly sanctioned a merger involving banking institutions, rather than remitting the matter to a lower court for further proceedings. What you should know Last September, Nairametrics reported that the two banks had secured the approval of their shareholders to merge, removing one of the hurdles to the process. When completed, the merged institution will debut with an extensive network of about 230 branches nationwide, immediately ranking it among the most expansive banks in Nigeria. Providus Bank brings its track record in innovation, digital banking, and customer-centric services, while Unity Bank contributes wide geographic reach and decades of brand equity. Combined, the lenders say they will be better positioned to support households, SMEs, corporates, and government institutions. The merged entity will also launch with a strong capital adequacy ratio, a crucial metric for competitiveness under Nigeria’s evolving banking reforms. Israel Ojoko Analyst 5 min read Follow Us on Google Discover Renaissance Capital (RenCap) has warned that Nigerian banks could be required to raise more than N1.7 trillion in fresh capital and undertake major restructuring of their group operations if the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) proceeds with its proposed Financial Holding Company (FHC) framework. In a report titled “ Nigerian Banks: More Capital, Declining Returns ” published on July 16, 2026 and obtained by Nairametrics, the investment bank warned that the apex bank’s proposal requiring holding companies to hold at least 20% capital above the sum of its subsidiaries’ paid-up capital could significantly dilute shareholder value and reduce returns on equity. According to RenCap, the proposal comes at a time when profitability across the banking sector is already moderating following record earnings recorded in recent years. What the report is saying RenCap argues that the proposed additional buffer is the most consequential aspect of the reforms and could become highly value-destructive for shareholders. The investment bank noted that because holding companies are non-operating entities, capital held at that level generates little or no return. “ Since HoldCo is a non-operating subsidiary, holding that much capital is a value-destruction play to providers of capital, ” RenCap added. According to the report, the impact would be even more severe for banking groups with extensive international operations that may be forced to adopt more complex holding company structures under the proposed framework. RenCap estimates that under its base-case scenario, several banking groups would need substantial capital injections to comply with the proposed rules. Among existing HoldCo structures, Access Holdings faces the largest capital requirement at N656.04 billion. Other estimated requirements include: First HoldCo – N135.03 billion FCMB Group – N112.84 billion GTCO – N56.02 billion Stanbic IBTC Holdings – N11.84 billion The report notes that Access Holdings would need to raise capital equivalent to nearly 50% of its market capitalization, making it the most impacted among existing HoldCos. By comparison, GTCO, Stanbic IBTC Holdings and First HoldCo would face relatively smaller funding gaps when measured against market value. RenCap noted that the draft framework contains no exemptions for banking groups operating outside formal HoldCo structures. Section 4.6 of the proposed guidelines requires closely linked entities to be consolidated under a single non-operating holding company, potentially bringing institutions such as Zenith Bank, United Bank for Africa (UBA), and Fidelity Bank within the scope of the new requirements. The report estimates their potential capital needs as follows: UBA – N416.01 billion Fidelity Bank – N188.83 billion Zenith Bank – N166.88 billion Measured against market capitalization, UBA would face the largest burden at approximately 23.1%, followed by Fidelity Bank at 15.3%, while Zenith Bank’s requirement would represent about 3.8% of its market value. Get up to speed The proposed guidelines represent the most significant review of Nigeria’s holding company framework since the original rules were introduced in 2014 following the transition away from universal banking. The CBN said its review was necessitated by gaps observed over a decade of implementation, including governance weaknesses, compliance inconsistencies, and operational inefficiencies. Under the draft framework, banking groups would be limited to two hierarchical layers and required to adopt one of two approved structures. Groups with international operations would operate under a two-tier structure, while primarily domestic groups would adopt a single-tier model. One of the most significant changes is the requirement that foreign subsidiaries be owned directly by the holding company rather than by the operating bank. This means banks currently operating international licences through their banking subsidiaries would be required to transfer ownership of offshore operations to the HoldCo level. More insights RenCap warned that the timing of the proposed reforms could further pressure shareholder returns. text: Close Home Exclusives Recapitalization Financial Analysis Corporate Stories Interviews Investigations Metrics Nairalytics Economy Business News Budget Public Debt Tax Markets Currencies Cryptos Commodities Equities Fixed Income Funds Management Securities Sectors Agriculture Aviation Company News Consumer Goods Corporate Updates Corporate deals Corporate Press Releases Energy Entertainment Financial Services Health Hospitality & Travel Manufacturing Real Estate and Construction Renewables & Sustainability Tech News Financial Literacy Career tips Personal Finance Lifestyle Billionaire Watch Profiles Opinions Blurb Market Views Op-Eds Research Analysis Search Financial Analysis September 6, 2026 Where will Wema Bank stock be in one year? Wema Bank has become a much bigger and more profitable bank in the past few years, while its shares have rallied sharply. Idika Aja Senior Analyst 3 min read Follow Us on Google Discover Wema Bank has become a much bigger and more profitable bank in the past few years, while its shares have rallied sharply. In 2025, it closed at N20.40, gaining over 124% and becoming the best-performing banking stock. By February 2026, it had joined the SWOOT club after its market capitalisation crossed N1 trillion. After another strong set of results, investors are faced with a different question: how much more can the stock deliver from here? The shares closed at N29.60 on Friday, September 4, 2026, giving Wema a market value of about N1.19 trillion. After gaining about 45% this year, the stock is already trading close to the upper end of its recent range, with a 52-week high of N36. So, the question is whether Wema can push beyond that level. Also Read NGX market cap hits N162 trillion for the first time ever NASD appoints Mrs. Arese Ugwu as new Acting Managing Director Best performing Equity mutual funds in Nigeria as of August 2026 At N29.60, the bank trades at just 3.93 times its trailing earnings. In simple terms, investors are paying less than N4 for every N1 Wema has earned over the trailing period. Its 44.4% return on equity also shows that the bank is generating a strong return from shareholders’ money. So, where could Wema Bank be in one year? The 3.93 times earnings valuation looks attractive, but it is based on what Wema has already earned. For someone buying the stock today, the bigger question is what the bank can deliver from here. Wema reported N6.55 in earnings per share for H1 2026. If the bank were to deliver a similar level in the second half, full-year EPS would be around N13.10. That would make the current N29.60 share price look increasingly attractive if the bank could sustain that level of earnings. But there are reasons to test that assumption before using it to value the stock. Can Wema sustain the earnings? In 2025, Wema’s H1 profit after tax was N87.5 billion, but full-year PAT rose to N194.5 billion. The bank therefore made considerably more in the second half. The EPS comparison is more complicated because Wema’s share count increased sharply during 2025. H1 2025 EPS was N8.17, compared with N7.13 for the full year, even though full-year profit was much higher. This means our N13.10 annualized EPS is a scenario, not a forecast. What matters is whether Wema can continue growing its profit quickly enough to translate that growth into higher earnings for each shareholder. There are encouraging signs; Wema’s net interest income increased 51% in H1 2026, while its loan book grew 22%. The bank is therefore making more from its core banking business. Its stronger balance sheet also gives it room to grow. Wema raised N200 billion in new capital, and management says it wants to use that capital to grow organically and move towards tier-one banking status within two to three years. The bank is also exploring opportunities in areas including power and the blue economy . That ambition has received some external support. Agusto & Co upgraded Wema’s rating to A, citing improvements in profitability, liquidity and capitalisation . The agency, however, warned that rapid loan growth could put the bank’s credit-risk management under greater pressure, and that warning is worth noting. Wema’s loans grew about 22% in H1, but customer deposits increased only 5%. The bank will need to attract more deposits as it expands lending. There is also the quality of earnings to consider. Trading income jumped sharply, while fee income fell about 20%. For the current earnings momentum to continue, Wema will need its core banking business to remain the main driver of growth. What could push the stock higher? The biggest catalyst is earnings; if Wema continues expanding its loan book, grows deposits, maintains strong credit quality and turns its larger capital base into higher profits, investors could become more willing to pay a higher price for the shares. Its digital banking business also provides another avenue for growth. Wema continues to invest in ALAT, while management is pursuing larger corporate relationships and new business opportunities. Wema has moved from a turnaround story to a growth story. At N29.60, and N45–N50 target represents roughly 52%–69% potential upside. That is a more measured expectation than the extraordinary gains the stock delivered over the past two years. Wema has already been one of the market’s biggest banking winners. The next year could extend that run. Idika Aja Senior Analyst 4 min read Follow Us on Google Discover VFD Group Plc has opened a N20 billion Commercial Paper (CP) issuance under its N50 billion Commercial Paper Programme. The offer, which opened on Friday, August 28, 2026, and closes on Friday, September 4, 2026, is expected to support the company’s short-term working capital needs and funding requirements. The issuance comes at a time when VFD Group is reporting stronger earnings performance, with profit after tax more than doubling in the first half of 2026. What the offer circular is saying Target Size: Up to N20 billion Series 2(A): 270-day tenor Series 2(B): 364-day tenor Discount Rate: 18.5498% (Series 2A) and 19.0383% (Series 2B) Implied Yield: 21.50% (Series 2A) and 23.50% (Series 2B) Settlement Date: September 7, 2026 Short-Term Rating: DataPro A1 Minimum Subscription: N5 million and multiples of N1 million thereafter The Company behind the offer VFD Group Plc operates as an investment company with interests spread across financial services, capital markets, technology, real estate, hospitality, media and entertainment, infrastructure and energy. What investors need to know Commercial Papers are short-term debt instruments that allow companies to raise funds directly from investors. However, unlike Federal Government-backed instruments such as Treasury Bills and bonds, commercial papers carry corporate credit risk because repayment depends on the financial strength and liquidity position of the issuing company. In simple terms, investors are lending money to VFD Group and expecting the company to repay the principal and agreed return at maturity. Therefore, investors must consider two key questions: First, does the return offered by VFD compensate investors for taking on corporate risk compared with lower-risk fixed-income alternatives? Second, does VFD Group have sufficient earnings, liquidity and balance sheet strength to repay investors when the CP matures? More Insight How attractive is VFD’s return compared with other fixed-income options? VFD Group’s Commercial Paper offers investors a premium return for accepting the additional risk associated with lending to a private company. The 270-day Series 2(A) offers an implied annual yield of 21.50%, while the longer 364-day Series 2(B) offers a higher yield of 23.50%. Based on the minimum subscription of N5 million, investors in the 270-day series pay approximately N4.31 million upfront and receive the full N5 million face value at maturity, generating a gross return of about N686,088. For the 364-day series, investors pay approximately N4.05 million upfront for a N5 million face value investment and earn a gross return of about N949,307 at maturity. Compared with government-backed fixed-income instruments, the yield represents the compensation investors receive for taking on corporate credit risk. At the 26 August 2026 Treasury Bills auction, the 364-day Treasury Bill cleared at a stop rate of 20.35%. This means VFD’s 364-day CP offers investors an additional 3.15 percentage points in annualised yield for accepting the risk associated with lending to a corporate issuer. The premium is also visible when compared with recent CBN OMO auction rates. At the 27 August 2026 OMO auction, stop rates settled at 19.85% for the 96-day instrument and 19.32% for the 152-day instrument, with a weighted average stop rate of 19.4064%. While Treasury Bills and OMO instruments benefit from government backing, VFD’s higher yield reflects the additional return investors demand for taking on issuer risk. However, the attractiveness of the yield must be assessed alongside VFD’s ability to repay investors Can VFD Group comfortably repay investors? For commercial paper investors, profitability alone is not enough. The key issue is whether the company has enough financial strength and liquidity to meet its obligation when the paper matures. Based on VFD Group’s latest financial performance, the company appears to have strengthened its repayment capacity, supported by improved earnings, stronger capitalisation and a sizeable investment portfolio. The company’s earnings performance provides the first positive signal. In H1 2026, profit after tax doubled to N10.1 billion, while gross earnings increased by about 30% to N53.7 billion. The improvement shows that VFD’s investment-led business model continues to generate stronger returns. More importantly for creditors, VFD’s balance sheet provides a reasonable cushion against the proposed borrowing. The company’s shareholders’ funds increased to approximately N124.9 billion, while borrowings stood at about N133.5 billion, translating to a debt-to-equity ratio of about 1.1x. text: Full Electronic Registration (e-Registration) now available on the ePortal | In a major boost to capital market regulation in Nigeria, President Ahmed Bola Tinubu GCFR, has assented to the Investments and Securities Bill (ISB) 2025, which repeals the Investments and Securities Act No. 29 of 2007 | Full Electronic Registration (e-Registration) now available on the ePortal | In a major boost to capital market regulation in Nigeria, President Ahmed Bola Tinubu GCFR, has assented to the Investments and Securities Bill (ISB) 2025, which repeals the Investments and Securities Act No. 29 of 2007 | Register a Company Published: August 14, 2023 Initiate company registration seamlessly with our platform, working in conjunction with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC). Transform your business dreams into a legal reality! Are you an enterprising entrepreneur in Nigeria looking to establish your business as a legal entity? Registering your company with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) is a vital step in the process. However, navigating the registration procedure can be intricate, especially if you are a first-time business owner. This in-depth guide aims to simplify the CAC registration process for you, ensuring you have all the necessary information to set your business on the path to success. Keep in mind that this page serves as a vital first step, preparing your business for potential registration as a capital market operator with the SEC. While our focus here is on CAC registration, it's a crucial foundational stage in your journey toward becoming a registered capital market operator. Section 1: Understanding CAC and Its Significance Exploring CAC and Its Crucial Role The Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) serves as the governmental body responsible for overseeing the formation and management of companies in Nigeria. Established under the Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA) in 1990, the CAC plays a pivotal role in the registration and regulation of companies and businesses operating within Nigeria. The primary reason for registering your company with the CAC is legal compliance. Nigerian law mandates all businesses to complete this process, and failure to do so can result in substantial fines, legal actions, and even the dissolution of your enterprise. CAC registration additionally extends legal protection to your company's name and brand, enhancing your capacity to safeguard intellectual property rights and prevent unauthorized usage of your brand identity. Section 2: Prerequisites for CAC Registration Step 1: Selecting a Distinct Company Name Commencing the registration process involves choosing an exclusive company name that does not infringe upon existing trademarks or company names. Verify the availability of your chosen name on the CAC Website or by visiting any CAC office nationwide. Step 2: Establishing an Account on the CAC Portal After confirming the name's availability, proceed to create an account on the CAC Registration Portal . This straightforward step necessitates the provision of personal details such as your name, email address, and phone number. Account creation is a fundamental prerequisite for company registration. Step 3: Completing the Online CAC Registration Form With your account in place, the next stage involves the completion of the online registration form on the portal. This form collects vital information about your company, including its name, address, directors, shareholders, and other pertinent details. Step 4: Submission of Required Documents In addition to form completion, you will be required to upload specified documents. These documents include your company's memorandum and articles of association, identification documents for directors and shareholders, and proof of your company's registered office address. Step 5: Settling Registration Fees Upon successful form submission and document uploads, the next step involves payment of registration fees . Fee structures differ based on your company's type and size, typically ranging from ₦10,000 to ₦50,000. Step 6: Monitoring Your Application Following submission and fee payment, you can track the progress of your application on the CAC portal. Regular updates regarding your application status, any supplementary document requests, or additional information will be provided. Step 7: Reception of Your Certificate of Incorporation Upon approval, you will receive your certificate of incorporation. This official document validates your company's registration with the CAC, featuring essential information about your company, such as its name, address, directors, and shareholders. Section 3: Post-CAC Registration Obligations Step 1: Attaining a Tax Identification Number (TIN) Post-CAC registration, securing a Tax Identification Number (TIN) from the Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS) is imperative. The TIN is indispensable for tax-related matters, bank account establishment, tax return filing, and various financial transactions. Step 2: Registration for Value-Added Tax (VAT) If your business involves the sale of goods or services, you may be required to register for Value-Added Tax (VAT) with the Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS). VAT is a tax levied on the value added to goods and services throughout production and distribution, typically at a rate of 5%. Step 3: Registration with Additional Regulatory Bodies Depending on your business's nature, you may need to register with other regulatory bodies such as the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC), the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), or the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN). This is where registration with us - the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) - comes in, if your business would involve the Nigerian capital market in any way. Conclusion The process of registering your business with the CAC may seem intricate, but it is a fundamental step in establishing your enterprise as a legitimate entity in Nigeria.
